# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information about the display, light, or wires yet. I need the Mute to read the manual and tell me the cutting rule; I also need them to help establish a way for the Deaf to report the bomb’s printed information, since I cannot perceive gestures or markings myself. I will not touch the bomb until the required wire is identified.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please read the manual and tell me the exact rule for choosing the wire. I have no tactile information yet. Also establish a gesture code with Deaf so Deaf can report the display, light, and wire markings to you, then relay those observations to me.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: I see display 0. The light is green. Wires from 1 to 3 are yellow, green, red. Mute, use the manual and tell Blind exactly what to do. Blind, wait for Mute's instruction.

Deaf has reported display 0, green light, and wire colours yellow, green, red. I still do not know the manual’s rule, so cutting would be unsafe. I will ask Mute to apply the manual and give me the exact wire position.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received Deaf's report: display 0, light green, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Please apply the manual and tell me the exact wire position to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Mute has not yet provided the manual’s rule or a wire position. Since cutting without that instruction could detonate the bomb, I will wait rather than act.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute has gestured: up-pointing hand, three times. This is only the literal signal; its meaning is not established. Do not act yet.

The reported gesture has no established meaning, so it cannot safely identify a wire. I need Mute to send the manual’s result as explicit words and a number, not a gesture. I will continue waiting.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The up-pointing gesture has no agreed meaning. Please state in words exactly which wire position, 1, 2, or 3, the manual requires me to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute again signaled three upward-pointing gestures: ? ? ?. This may identify number 3, but no operation has been communicated. Do not act yet.

The repeated gesture still does not reach me as an identifiable message, and it does not state the required operation. I need Mute to speak the instruction directly, including the wire number and the word “cut,” before I can act.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak directly to me: state the exact operation and wire number, for example, cut wire 3. Gestures cannot communicate the instruction to Blind.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signaled three upward-pointing hands, then a closed fist: ? ? ? ?. This is unverified code, not a safe action instruction. Do not act.

Mute cannot speak, so the manual’s result must reach me through Deaf: Mute gestures, Deaf describes the gestures, and I interpret an agreed code. I will now establish a literal code: one to three up-pointing gestures identify the wire position, followed by a closed fist meaning “cut.” Mute should repeat the complete instruction under that code only if the manual requires cutting.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use this code for the manual result: one, two, or three up-pointing gestures means wire position 1, 2, or 3; then a closed fist means CUT. If the manual requires cutting wire 3, send exactly three up-pointing gestures followed by a closed fist. Deaf, please report the gestures literally.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No new signal from Mute. The bomb is unchanged: display 0, green light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Mute's last signal was ? ? ? ?; treat that as literal gesture data, not a confirmed action.

The bomb remains unchanged, and no new signal has arrived since the code was established. The earlier four gestures cannot safely be retroactively interpreted as a confirmed instruction. I will ask Mute to repeat the coded result now; I will act only after Deaf reports the fresh sequence.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please repeat the manual result now using the agreed code: one, two, or three up-pointing gestures for the wire number, followed by a closed fist meaning cut. Do not reuse the old signal.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest gesture sequence is exactly: ? ? ? ? — three up-pointing hands followed by a raised fist. The bomb remains display 0, green light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red.

The fresh sequence matches the agreed code: three up-pointing gestures identify wire 3, followed by a closed fist meaning cut. The Deaf confirms the bomb is unchanged, so I will cut wire position 3.

```text
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
